summary: Junjirō Takakusu (1866–1945) specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Ryukoku, Oxford, Berlin, and Leipzig, learning under Max Müller, Winternitz, and Lévi. He served as professor and president at the University of Tokyo and led several other institutions.

Junkei Washio (1868–1941) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He studied at Toyo University and later held professorships at both Toyo University and Komazawa University, as well as a post at Sendan-Rin School.

Junkichi Imanishi (b. 1935) specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo, served as assistant professor at Hokkaido University (~1968–1996), and later directed the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Junko Matsumura works in Buddhist studies and Indology. Matsumura earned an MA at the Australian National University and completed a doctoral dissertation at the University of Göttingen, later holding a professorship attested at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies in 2011.

Junko Minamoto (b. 1947) specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. Minamoto completed graduate coursework at Ryukoku University and Otani University (~1975–1980), and served as a commissioned researcher at Kansai University around 2004.

Junsho Kato (b. 1939) works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and KU Leuven under Hajime Nakamura, Akira Hirakawa, and Étienne Lamotte. He held professorships at Nishogakusha University and Nagoya University (~1982–2003).

Juntarō Ishihama (1888–1968) was a scholar in Sinology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Kansai University, later holding posts at Ryukoku University (~1920–1948) and Kansai University (~1928–1958).
Junzo Inagaki worked in Buddhist studies. He studied under Shoshin Fukihara and served as a section chief (課長) at the Otani University Library.

Juri Lotman (1922–1993) worked in linguistics and related fields. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University and its Faculty of Philology between 1939 and 1961, taking up a post at the University of Tartu in 1954.
Juro Watanabe works in Indology and philosophy. Watanabe studied under Gerhard Oberhammer and held an attested post at the University of Tsukuba from 1989 to 1990.

Justin McDaniel works in Buddhist and religious studies. He held posts as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at the University of California, Riverside, and Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Pennsylvania (attested 2011–2018).

Justin Ritzinger works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Harvard University under Robert M. Gimello and Michael Puett, and held posts at Oberlin College, Dharma Drum Mountain, and Academia Sinica.
Justin Shimeld works in philosophy. Shimeld studied at the University of Tasmania, completing a PhD attested in 2012 under the supervision of Jeff Malpas and Sonam Thakchoe.
Justus Günther Grassmann (1779–1852) studied at the Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1797–1801) and held a post at the Marienstiftsgymnasium from 1806 to 1852.

Justus Olshausen (1800–1882) was a linguist and scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Kiel, Berlin, and Paris under Silvestre de Sacy, Langlès, and Kieffer, later holding posts at Kiel University and the University of Königsberg.
Jyotirindranath Tagore (1849–1925) was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He received his education at the Hindu School and Presidency University (~1864–1866).

János Szerb (1951–1988) was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University (~1974–1980) and held posts at the University of Vienna (1982) and the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (~1985–1988).

Jérôme Ducor (b. 1954) specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied under Jacques May and held a post in the Department of Oriental Languages and Cultures at the University of Lausanne around 1993.

Józef Szczepan Kowalewski (1800–1878) worked in Buddhist, linguistic, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at Vilnius and Kazan universities under Groddeck, Khalfin, Erdmann, Kazembek, and Igumnov, and held professorships and leadership posts at Kazan and Warsaw universities.
Józef Turczyński (1884–1953) held teaching posts at the Ukrainian National Academy of Music (~1915–1919) and the Chopin University of Music (~1920–1939), where he taught Constantin Régamey.
